AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: Evaluate the relationship between subjective knee function and lower extremity strength in individuals with patellofemoral pain(PFP).

AbstractText.Label: PARTICIPANTS
AbstractText.content: Participants were 30 individuals with PFP (20 females, 10 males; 76.02±17.88kg, 173.04±7.58cm, 24.9±7years).

AbstractText.Label: MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES
AbstractText.content: Subjects completed the Activities of Daily Living Scale(ADLS) and had lower extremity hip and knee isometric strength assessed. Strength was compared between low and high subjective function ADLS groups. Correlations for strength and subjective function were assessed; with a linear regression utilized to determine if strength predicted subjective function.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Quadriceps strength was significantly greater in the high subjective function group 38.5±13.9%BM than low subjective function: 27.88±8.96%BM, p=.02. Significant correlations were seen between the ADLS and all five lower extremity strength measures(r=0.376-0.535). Quadriceps strength was a strong predictor of subjective function in those with PFP, explaining 28.6% of the total variance in the ADLS.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Quadriceps strength was a strong predictor of subjective function when assessed by the ADLS PFP patients and significantly greater in those with higher subjective function. A strong relationship exists between self-reported function and lower extremity strength, suggesting the need to evaluate and treat lower extremity weakness.
